name: Mental-health and therapy practices (admin)

problems.words: Late cancellations leave practitioners with empty hours
quick_ideas: Count late cancellations per practitioner for a week, so the loss is measured
Make sure every client has seen the cancellation policy, so it is clear.

workzap_build.text: online booking per practitioner with reminders and a policy acknowledgement at booking, tracking cancellations automatically.

problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and policy flow are in the solution document.

problems.words: We have a long waitlist but some practitioners still have gaps
quick_ideas: List waitlist requests by service type, language and availability, so matches are easier
Compare that with practitioners' open hours, so gaps can be offered.

workzap_build.text: a waitlist and matching board showing open requests and time on list, offering freed slots to matched clients.

problems.free_stops: Matching rules are in the solution document.

never_say: Any therapy, counselling, diagnosis, crisis or medication advice, including "what staff should say".
Anything about a client's situation, even in general terms.
Interpretations of confidentiality or record-keeping law.
Help sharing records without consent or issuing letters without proper sessions.
Ideas that record client names, reasons for seeking help or session content.
If anyone mentions suicide, self-harm or danger: emergency services first (and 9-8-8 in Canada).

sample_reply.person: Late cancellations are killing us. Therapists lose hours every week and we never charge the fee. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be brought under control, and you can start this week. 1) Count late cancellations per therapist for a week, so the lost time is measured. 2) Make sure every client has seen the cancellation policy, so it is clear before it is needed. Workzap can do this automatically for you with online booking, reminders, policy acknowledgement and a log of fees due. Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're welcome to say no.
